questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy stocks a hydrocodone-only extended release product that is not formulated in an abuse deterrent form. The pharmacist on duty is working out how the regulation treats that product where support personnel are concerned. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The prohibition turns on whether the product is in an abuse deterrent form.
The prohibition reaches every extended release opioid product the pharmacy stocks.
It reaches pharmacy technician trainees as well as licensed and certified technicians.
Pharmacist approval evidenced by written policies and procedures permits a certified technician to handle it.
A hydrocodone-only extended release product in an abuse deterrent form falls outside the prohibition.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is behind on continuing education for the current calendar year. She attends an intensive live conference held on a single day in December and the authorized provider issues her a statement of credit for 12 contact hours earned that day. She wants to apply all 12 to that calendar year. How many of those contact hours may she apply?

choices.text: The full 12, because the daily restriction applies to home study rather than live programs.
The full 12, because live conference programming carries no daily restriction.
Ten, because a registrant may not exceed ten contact hours in a calendar day.
None, because contact hours earned in December are credited to the following cycle.
Eight, because a registrant may not earn more than eight contact hours in a calendar day.
